review_scope: Independent post-repair audit of CLAIMS_AUDIT.json and PROOF_DEPENDENCIES.json against main.tex, extracted main.pdf text in main.txt, PDF_VALIDATION.json, SOURCE_MANIFEST.json, and the stated truth-boundary criteria.
reviewer_separation: This review accepted the Engineer repair as an input artifact and performed no repair edits to claim or dependency files.
basis: main.tex states exactly one theorem and six propositions whose labels and numbering match CLAIMS_AUDIT.json proof_location fields and PROOF_DEPENDENCIES.json node IDs.

The Route A computational propositions explicitly state their finite algebraic objects, rational domains, root/sign methods, coverage limits, and nonclaims; no program exit code is used alone as proof.

The Route B propositions state the RR/H313 hypotheses, Delta_G strata, endpoint sign arguments, one-way Y=0 crossing obstruction, and surviving open packets without promoting them to finite-cyclicity or Hilbert-number theorems.
PDF_VALIDATION.json reports main.pdf exists, has readable extracted text, parses required JSON artifacts, and contains the title, open-problem language, rho=200, Delta_G, Y=0, and limitations checks.
SOURCE_MANIFEST.json lists 26 claim-bearing inputs with SHA-256 hashes and sizes, and the paper includes the generated source hash appendix.
open_gaps_confirmed: Hilbert's sixteenth problem, Part II, remains open.
No degree-wise uniform finiteness theorem is proved.
Route A remains a finite selected local atlas/tube and successor-wall certification, not a global degree-six theorem.
Route B leaves the direct H313 Type-II packet and invariant-line endpoint-matched Dulac/anchor packet open.
No global gluing theorem is supplied.
